title: publish-release.sh install smoke fails ETARGET over a complete rc publish: gate reads npm view, smoke reads npx's packument
description: Measured by opum-doc on the 0.15.0 rc staging, 2026-11-02: the in-script npx smoke ran at 19:55:00Z, 8s after wait_for_all_visible passed, failed ETARGET (No matching version found for @opum-ai/lore@0.15.0-rc.1) and the script exited non-zero over a complete, correct publish (six platforms and the launcher, sha256 matching the qualified digests; publish-release.sh 0.15.0 41321407675 --verify-only at 7b617684 exits 0). Confirmed from the script at v0.15.0 (scripts/publish-release.sh, identical on origin/dev 79988dd8): the gate probes `npm view <spec> version` once per package (spec_visible, line 1001), then the smoke runs ONE `npx --yes @opum-ai/lore@<rc>` (line 1486) and dies on any non-zero (lines 1489-1492). The comment at 1489 asserts a post-gate failure "is NOT propagation", and that premise is false: the two reads are not the same read (npx/npm resolve through a cached or differently-propagated packument). Consequence: a failing exit and a "the install path is broken, investigate" message over a good release, and a re-run refuses with "already exists", which pushes toward unpublish. Fix direction, not implemented here: retry the smoke inside the remaining visibility window with backoff, and/or bypass the cache (e.g. --prefer-online or a fresh cache dir) before reporting failure; correct the wrong comment and failure wording; keep a genuine failure after the window loud. Evidence for the design: reproduce locally only (unit test of the retry with a stub npx, local registry); any real publish is the operator tier-3 action. scripts/ and release.yml changes need a reviewer pass before landing.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A smoke that fails with ETARGET (or an equivalent not-yet-resolvable error) is retried with backoff within the registry window before the script reports failure; a test using a stubbed npx that fails N times then succeeds exits 0
A smoke that still fails after the window exits non-zero with wording that does not assert the failure cannot be propagation, and does not invite unpublish
The smoke bypasses npx's cached packument (or the retry demonstrably outlasts it), pinned by a test on the argv or environment the script builds
The comment at the smoke site no longer claims a post-gate failure is not propagation
Reviewer pass on the scripts/ change recorded before it lands
